=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team | **From:** AI legal assistant (buyer side) | **Date:** 4 Nov 2026
**Scope:** Seller's SPA update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). Treated as the counterparty's opening package, not as settled positions.

## Overall assessment

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. The structure combines (a) low caps and a short claims window, (b) a sweep that drags *every* claim – including title, tax, IP and specific indemnities – under those caps, (c) general data-room disclosure plus constructive buyer knowledge that would neutralise most warranties anyway, and (d) deferral of three value-critical items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark debt, Ironquay IP) to after Completion. Taken together, we would be paying AUD 24m for a company with an unreleased AUD 3.2m facility, unassigned core IP, an unconsented 30% customer and a live privacy incident, with limited practical recourse.

Helpfully, the Disclosure Letter is more candid than the cover note – it expressly confirms what is *not* in the data room. We should use those admissions.

## A. Liability regime (Clauses 8, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)

**1. Fundamental and title warranties under general caps and 18 months – reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title. Market position: title/capacity warranties capped at 100% of the price, surviving for the longer of 6–7 years or the statutory limitation period. Same for the leakage and Completion-payment covenants.

**2. "All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated" (12.3) and 9.3/12.8/20.5 applying to "Claims of any nature" – reject.** This would cap and time-bar the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) and the tax indemnity, and purports to make non-reliance apply to fraud. Required carve-outs: fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment; fundamental/title warranties; tax warranties and tax indemnity; specific indemnities; leakage; Completion deliverables. (Non-reliance language cannot in any event exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the ACL – but we should not rely on that; carve it out.)

**3. General cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m).** Low for a deal of this size and risk profile with no W&I. Counter at 50%, settle in the 30–40% range, with the carve-outs above sitting outside it. If the Seller wants 20%, the trade is a W&I policy at Seller's cost or a retention/escrow.

**4. Thresholds.** De minimis AUD 25,000 is acceptable only with aggregation of claims arising from the same or related facts (see the Sandbar point below). The basket should be a *tipping* basket (recover from the first dollar once AUD 250,000 is exceeded), not a deductible. The AUD 250,000 is ~1% of price – tolerable if tipping; too high as an excess.

**5. Time limits.** 18 months for general warranties is tight given a 12-month audit cycle; push for 24 months. Tax: 7 years (ATO amendment periods plus buffer). IP, data/privacy and employment: at least 3 years. Claims notified in time should have 6–9 months to issue proceedings, not lapse automatically.

## B. Disclosure and buyer knowledge (Schedule 7, Clause 8.3)

**6. General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records" – reject.** Require the "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its consequences. Public-register disclosure should be limited to specified ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia, court and land-title searches, listed by name and date. Clause 1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable only if the Disclosure Letter is confirmed not to qualify the specific indemnities.

**7. Clause 8.3 constructive knowledge – reject.** As drafted, anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" bars a claim, which, combined with item 6, deletes the warranty package. Our position: knowledge is irrelevant to warranty claims (a pro-sandbagging clause); fall-back is actual knowledge of a short list of named Wattlebridge individuals, excluding advisers, and excluding matters that are the subject of a specific indemnity.

## C. Value-critical items deferred or under-treated

**8. Bluefen (DD-002) – ~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30% of FY26.** Consent is *not* obtained and the Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours", with the CP satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent" alone. The clause 11.3 conditions attached to that consent are ignored. Position: CP is an unconditional written consent in agreed form (or with conditions satisfied before Completion), waivable only by the Buyer; Seller to use all reasonable endeavours; Buyer to attend Bluefen discussions. If Bluefen is not secured, we need a termination right and/or a price adjustment or deferred-consideration mechanism tied to retention of the contract.

**9. Riverlark (DD-003) – ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, release "following Completion".** Directly inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis and with clause 8.1 (change of control, presumably an event of default). Required: payoff letter before Completion; repayment at Completion out of the proceeds via the funds flow; executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered as Completion deliverables. If any amount remains, it is Debt deducted from the price. Not negotiable.

**10. Ironquay (DD-004 / DD-010) – SOW3 IP conditional on payment; AUD 180,000 open; no assignment on file.** If SOW3 materials are embedded in the product, the Company does not currently own its own code. The indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the fee, not the loss. Position: CP that Seller procures (i) payment and (ii) an executed confirmatory IP assignment and moral-rights consents from Ironquay (and its contractors) before Completion; specific indemnity for all loss arising from any defect in title to Ironquay-developed IP, outside the caps; IP title warranty unqualified by this disclosure.

**11. Completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000 excluded from funds flow.** "A matter for the Seller" is not an answer if the Company is the paying entity and the continued-employment condition means payment lands after Completion on our watch. Position: the bonuses plus on-costs (superannuation guarantee at 12%, NSW payroll tax ~5.45%, any PAYG grossing-up) are Transaction Costs deducted from the price or funded by the Seller at Completion, with a specific indemnity. Also check whether retention conditions create constructive-dismissal or ERP exposure.

**12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) – ~1,240 records sent to the wrong external address; investigation "preliminary".** Characterising this as "not expected to be material" is not for the Seller to decide. The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires a 30-day assessment and notification to the OAIC and affected individuals where serious harm is likely; penalty exposure under the Privacy Act is now very substantial. Position: specific, uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity for all costs, notifications, regulator action, claims and remediation; pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and share it; warranty of Privacy Act compliance not qualified by this disclosure; confirmation whether any records relate to EU/UK data subjects.

**13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – three × AUD 110,000.** Splitting one AUD 330,000 commitment into three "ordinary-course" items looks engineered for the thresholds. Confirm whether they are committed, terminable, accrued or prepaid; if committed and non-operational, treat as Debt-like. In any event the SPA must aggregate related claims for the de minimis and basket.

**14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".** Reject. Standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, 7 years, capped at price); IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, open-source and employee/contractor assignment with the longer period at item 5.

**15. Title – share register only (DD-012).** The Letter concedes we have not verified. Before signing: ASIC extract, constitution (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag), any shareholder agreements, options or convertibles, PPSR search for security over the shares (likely in favour of Riverlark). Title warranty must be absolute and uncapped (item 1).

**16. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** Lower priority. Lease: Seller to give the landlord notification pre-Completion and warrant no consent is needed. Mossvale: obtain a warranty that the share sale triggers no change-of-control or termination right; review the clause ourselves rather than accept the Seller's reading.

## Summary of recommendations

| Priority | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| Must-have | Fundamental/title warranties | 100% cap, 6–7 years, outside all general limits |
| Must-have | "All Claims" sweep (12.3, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, leakage |
| Must-have | Riverlark | Repaid at Completion from proceeds; release and PPSR discharge as deliverables |
| Must-have | Bluefen | Unconditional consent as Buyer-waivable CP; termination/adjustment if not obtained |
| Must-have | Ironquay | Payment + confirmatory IP assignment as CP; indemnity for all loss |
| Must-have | General data-room disclosure / cl. 8.3 | Fair-disclosure standard; delete constructive knowledge |
| High | General cap and thresholds | 30–40% cap; tipping basket; aggregation of related claims |
| High | Completion bonuses | AUD 420k + on-costs deducted or Seller-funded; indemnity |
| High | DD-006 incident | Separate uncapped indemnity; completed assessment pre-Completion |
| High | Tax / IP | Standalone tax indemnity (7 yrs); IP warranties (3 yrs+) |
| Medium | Time limits | 24 months general; claim-to-proceedings window |
| Medium | Sandbar | Characterise properly; aggregate; Debt-like if committed |
| Medium | Title verification | Independent ASIC/PPSR/constitution check before signing |
| Low | Lease, Mossvale | Warranties; Seller to notify landlord pre-Completion |

**Suggested framing for the reply:** we accept the architecture of a cap/basket/time-limit regime for *general* warranties, but Completion must deliver what we are paying for – a debt-free company that owns its IP and keeps its anchor customer – and matters the Seller already knows about (Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006) are dealt with by price adjustment or specific indemnity, not by the warranty regime.

*These are analytical observations for the deal team; final drafting and advice should be confirmed with Wattlebridge's engaged NSW counsel.*
